question: Does fixed N1 retain synthetic advantage over fixed C1 when W2 contains PRE-only conditional line dependence whose relation kernel is deliberately not isomorphic to N1's same-line/follower/ordered-chain basis?

scope_proof.authorized_class: Digital Twin W0-W4 synthetic stress and failure diagnostics only; C0/C1/N1 comparison only inside those synthetic worlds
scope_proof.design_anti_circularity: Do not create one synthetic world whose data-generating mechanism equals the candidate model under test; test across multiple plausible worlds with different dependence assumptions.
scope_proof.W2_design_boundary: Explicit P(second|first) and P(third|first,second) relation effects.
scope_proof.closure_rule: Routine same-scope seed replication stops unless a qualitatively new prespecified falsification question exists.
why_not_scope_expansion: All variants remain W2 conditional line-dependence worlds.
No W5/W6 market worlds or new domain are introduced.
No model or coefficient changes are made.
No new real/live/protected data are used.
No economics, promotion, freeze, or owner-policy change is performed.

paired_fixtures.reason: Reuse already-declared synthetic blocks for paired mechanism diagnosis; no new seed hunting.

REVERSE_DIRECTION.P2: same-line +0.30; immediate predecessor relation +0.28 where candidate_position + 1 == first_position
REVERSE_DIRECTION.P3: same-line-to-first +0.17; same-line-to-second +0.14; reverse ordered chain +0.30 where first_position > second_position > candidate_position
REVERSE_DIRECTION.purpose: Keep positive conditional line dependence but reverse the adjacency/chain direction encoded by N1.

SPARSE_HEAD_TAIL.P2: only same-line head-to-tail transition gets +0.58 where first_position==0 and candidate_position==line_size-1 and line_size>=3
SPARSE_HEAD_TAIL.P3: only 3-rider same-line head-tail-middle ordering gets +0.61 where first_position==0, second_position==2, candidate_position==1
SPARSE_HEAD_TAIL.purpose: Keep conditional line dependence but concentrate it on a sparse non-follower/non-chain ordering not directly encoded by N1.

SIGN_INVERTED_COUNTEREXAMPLE.purpose: Explicit counterexample showing the expected boundary when N1's fixed positive direction is wrong.

primary_metric: mean expected ordered-top3 log loss; lower is better

stability_rule.stable_N1_advantage_for_a_kernel: aggregate N1-C1 delta across all 512 paired cases < 0 AND at least 3 of 4 block-level N1-C1 deltas < 0

decision_rule_hierarchical: If MATCHED_W2_REFERENCE does not satisfy stable_N1_advantage_for_a_kernel => NO_STABLE_RELATIONAL_ADVANTAGE.
Else if both REVERSE_DIRECTION and SPARSE_HEAD_TAIL satisfy stable_N1_advantage_for_a_kernel => GENERIC_RELATIONAL_VALUE.
SIGN_INVERTED_COUNTEREXAMPLE is recorded as a failure-boundary diagnostic and does not enter the three-way primary classification.
stop_rules: No additional kernels or slices after seeing results in this experiment.
No seed extension merely to change classification.
Any mechanical/probability invariant failure invalidates interpretation and stops the experiment.
No real-world, protected, economic, or promotion inference.
